questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How Apple designed the Macintosh after two visits to PARC
The Xerox Alto, an influential but unsuccessful early GUI computer
The history of the computer mouse from SRI to the ball mouse
How Xerox built and sold its Star office system for $100,000
questions.explain: The passage covers the Alto's history, influence and architecture, noting it did not succeed commercially but influenced later systems.

questions.q: About how many Alto systems were produced in total?
options: About 30
About 500
About 1,000
About 2,000

questions.q: Who was awarded the 2009 Turing Award for the Alto's design?
options: Butler Lampson
Charles P. Thacker
Alan C. Kay
Douglas Engelbart
questions.explain: Charles P. Thacker received the 2009 Turing Award for his pioneering design and realization of the Alto.

questions.q: Why was the Alto's Ethernet designed to run at 3 Mbit/s?
options: The microcode engine could not go faster and still run display, disk and refresh
Xerox wanted it to match the speed of the IBM equipment of the time
The Alto's three-button mouse could not handle any faster signaling
The coaxial cables of the era could not reliably carry more than that
questions.explain: The speed was set because the microcode engine could not go faster and still support video, disk activity and memory refresh.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the Alto's impact on Apple?
options: Apple copied its mouse design from the Alto's five-key chord keyset
Apple bought Xerox's Star design in 1981 and rebranded it as Lisa
Apple used ideas seen in demonstrations to develop the Lisa and Macintosh
Apple refused every visit to PARC and designed its GUI alone
questions.explain: After Jobs arranged visits to see the Alto in 1979, Apple engineers used the concepts in developing the Lisa and Macintosh.
